Twenty
twĕn'tŭ
n. and a. (twice ten; in the Law, the age at which a man is numbered, taxed, and mustered)
From Anglo-Saxon twentig — twain plus -tig, a group of ten; literally two tens. The Hebrew esrim is likewise the plural of eser, ten.

Biblical Definition

Twenty is the threshold number of the Law. “Every one that passeth among them that are numbered, from twenty years old and above, shall give an offering unto the LORD” (Exo 30:14) — at twenty a man enters the census, pays the atonement money, and becomes liable to the muster of war. Twenty is the age at which Israel stops counting a man as a child and starts counting him as one of the people, with a name in the roll and a half shekel to render. That cuts both ways: the wilderness generation condemned at Kadesh is reckoned “from twenty years old and upward” (Num 14:29), so the same threshold that confers standing confers accountability. Twenty appears again in the pleading of Abraham, where it is the second-to-last step of his descent: “Peradventure there shall be twenty found there” (Gen 18:31) — and the LORD grants it, as He grants every step, because the whole exchange is a lesson in how far mercy will go when it is asked.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines twenty as twice ten, and observes that it is used proverbially for an indefinite number, as when we say a thing has been done twenty times.

expand to see more

TWENTY, a. Twice ten; as twenty men; twenty years.

2. Proverbially, an indefinite number. He has done it twenty times.

TWENTY, n. The number of twenty; twice ten.

Note. In the Mosaic law, twenty years is the age at which a male is enrolled and numbered among the people.

Key Scripture

Exo 30:14 — "Every one that passeth among them that are numbered, from twenty years old and above, shall give an offering unto the LORD."

Gen 18:31 — "And he said, Behold now, I have taken upon me to speak unto the Lord: Peradventure there shall be twenty found there. And he said, I will not destroy it for twenty's sake."

Exo 30:13 — "This they shall give, every one that passeth among them that are numbered, half a shekel after the shekel of the sanctuary: (a shekel is twenty gerahs:) an half shekel shall be the offering of the LORD."

Num 4:3 — "From thirty years old and upward even until fifty years old, all that enter into the host, to do the work in the tabernacle of the congregation."

Modern Corruption

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition; what is lost is the older instinct that a man arrives at a definite age with definite obligations attached.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Nobody disputes the meaning of twenty. What has quietly disappeared is the thing the number does in the Law: mark a line at which a man is enrolled, taxed, and mustered, and after which the excuses of boyhood are no longer available to him. Exo 30:14 hands the twenty-year-old a bill he must pay in person — the same half shekel from rich and poor — and Num 14:29 hands the same generation a judgment it cannot shift onto its parents.

The principle to recover is that Scripture attaches responsibility to an age and expects men to arrive there. A culture that stretches adolescence into the late twenties has not been kinder to its young men; it has withheld from them the standing Exodus grants at twenty. Fathers and elders serve them best by naming the threshold plainly and putting real weight on the other side of it.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew esrim (H6242), twenty, the plural of eser, ten; the age of enrolment in the Mosaic census and of liability to the atonement money.

expand to see more

Hebrew esrim (H6242) — twenty; grammatically the plural of eser, ten, as the Hebrew tens are all formed.

Hebrew gerah (H1626) — the smallest weight; twenty gerahs make the sanctuary shekel (Exo 30:13), so twenty is also a standard of the sanctuary's own reckoning.

Greek eikosi (G1501) — twenty; used of the four and twenty elders of Rev 4:4.

The muster formula — “from twenty years old and upward, all that are able to go forth to war” (Num 1:3) recurs through the census chapters as a fixed legal phrase.

The judgment formula — the same threshold defines who dies in the wilderness (Num 14:29); standing and accountability are granted together.

Usage

"“From twenty years old and above” — the age of enrolment, taxation, and muster."

"“A shekel is twenty gerahs” — twenty as a standard of sanctuary weight."

"“For twenty's sake” — the second-to-last step of Abraham's pleading, and granted."
